pattern_updates.reason: RB47 now resolves to a precise archival-address candidate while raw measurements remain absent; Nimitz has an official short-retention CIC-log authority in the historical records regime; Tehran has a dense U.S. reporting/advisory shadow without recovered instrument records. The report layer repeatedly survives more robustly than replayable geometry.

NARA N1-NU-89-005 explicitly assigns SSIC 3560/1 Combat Information Center Logs a three-year retention and DAA-NU-2015-0003 later lists that authority among superseded Navy schedules. This establishes a concrete ordinary short-retention pathway in the correct operational neighborhood, although mapping raw AN/SPY-1 products to that class remains unresolved.
No recovered artifact supplies common-time calibrated fusion for RB47, Nimitz or Tehran.
R4 added archive/custody precision, not measurement uncertainty. Reported numerical values still cannot be promoted to error-bounded state vectors.
Tehran's U.S. reporting infrastructure is now better bounded, but no F-4 maintenance/fault record was recovered to validate the reported instrumentation effects.
No synchronized target/interceptor state vectors were recovered.

new_relationships.relation: Short-lived operational log/data classes provide an ordinary mechanism by which later investigators retain testimony and summaries from multiple channels but lose the common-time electronic records required to fuse those channels.
When summaries survive after raw records disappear, exact-looking numbers can persist detached from sensor mode, calibration and covariance, making narrative precision outlive physical accuracy.

provenance_updates.finding: Candidate archive reference 6961835 plus Blue Book case number 4810 and T-1206 locator materially narrow retrieval, but identifier namespaces remain distinct and the direct NARA byte bind is still open.
Routine short retention is now documented in the relevant Navy operational-record neighborhood. No evidence yet maps specific Princeton raw track products to SSIC 3560/1 or proves their destruction.

RG59 CFPF plus the large FY1976 U.S. security-assistance presence create a deterministic American documentary-shadow search surface, but no event-specific new telegram or maintenance record has been recovered.

canonical_seal: THE NEW REPEATABLE STRUCTURE IS STILL IN THE EVIDENCE PIPELINE, NOT IN THE MACHINE. UNTIL TWO CASES SHARE A CALIBRATED PHYSICAL SIGNATURE, COMMON ORIGIN REMAINS UNNECESSARY.
